page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-56 is a compute-focused server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It features 56 vCPUs mapped to 28 physical cores with multithreading enabled, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 224 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance does not include local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it does not bundle complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and memory performance. The instance achieves top-tier status in PassMark memory testing and small-model LLM text generation. Multi-core performance is strong, as evidenced by high scores in stress-ng multi-core CPU tests, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU tests. Cryptographic and physics simulations also perform in the top 25%. However, single-core performance, large-block memory bandwidth, and static web serving throughput remain in the average tier.

From a resource density perspective, the c2d-standard-56 offers a balanced compute-to-memory ratio suitable for parallelized workloads without the premium cost of memory-optimized configurations. The lack of local SSD storage represents a tradeoff, requiring network-attached storage for disk-heavy operations. The instance is suited for software compilation, ray tracing, image processing, database operations, and medium-scale LLM text generation.
